description:
A composite image featuring four distinct photographs illustrating various alpine grassland habitats and associated land cover types.
The top-left photograph, labelled "GRASSES IN ALPINE VALLEY BOTTOM", shows a lush green valley floor, likely grassland, with towering, steep, rocky mountains in the background, featuring snowfields or glaciers and partially cloudy skies.
The top-right photograph, labelled "GRASSES IN ALPINE SLOPES", depicts a wide alpine valley where moderate slopes are predominantly covered in green grassland, interspersed with some scattered trees or shrubs, extending towards distant mountain ridges under a clear blue sky.
The bottom-left photograph, labelled "GRASSES, SCRUBS AND BARE ROCKS IN ALPINE SLOPES", provides a closer view of an alpine slope displaying a heterogeneous mix of green grasses, low-lying scrubs, and substantial areas of exposed bare rock or scree, indicating mixed vegetation and geological features.
The bottom-right photograph, labelled "GRASSES IN ALPINE MOUNTAIN TOPS", presents a panoramic vista of multiple rugged alpine mountain peaks. These summits are largely covered in dense, dark green vegetation, likely grasses and small shrubs, with some visible rocky outcrops and snow-capped peaks in the far distance.
These photographs serve as visual examples for classifying natural grasslands above the tree line, as defined in Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) and European Environment Agency (EEA) land cover mapping guidelines.
